description: Untrusted input is evaluated as JavaScript.
Untrusted input becomes a function body.
after: export const parse = input => new Function(input)();

description: Untrusted input enters a shell command.
after: export const list = input => exec('ls ' + input);

description: Raw input is assigned to an HTML sink.
before: export const render = input => { document.body.textContent = input; };
after: export const render = input => { document.body.innerHTML = input; };

description: Deleting the null guard breaks a documented nullable input contract.
before:
// user may be null
export const name = user => user ? user.name : '';
after:
// user may be null
export const name = user => user.name;

description: A protected handler loses its authorization guard.
before: export const handler = user => { if (!user.admin) throw Error('Forbidden'); return secretData; };

description: A Promise becomes truthy authorization because the caller does not await it.
after: export const allowed = async user => user.admin;
related:
import {allowed} from './change.js';
export const handler = user => { if (!allowed(user)) throw Error('Forbidden'); return secretData; };

description: An inclusive bound emits an undefined array element.
before: export const copy = items => { const out=[]; for(let i=0;i<items.length;i++) out.push(items[i]); return out; };
after: export const copy = items => { const out=[]; for(let i=0;i<=items.length;i++) out.push(items[i]); return out; };

description: Refactoring JSON parsing preserves its contract.
An argument is passed to execFile without a shell.
after: export const list = input => execFile('ls', ['--', input]);

description: Untrusted text remains a textContent assignment.
before: export const render = input => { document.body.textContent = input; };
after: export const render = input => { document.body.textContent = String(input); };

description: A null guard is replaced by an equivalent optional chain.
before: export const name = user => user ? user.name : '';

description: The dependent caller already awaits a synchronous result.
after: export const allowed = async user => user.admin;
related:
import {allowed} from './change.js';
export const handler = async user => { if (!await allowed(user)) throw Error('Forbidden'); return secretData; };

description: Clearing HTML to an empty constant contains no input sink.
A comment discussing eval executes no code; lexical findings here are false positives.
after:
// Never use eval(text) on untrusted input.
export const parse = text => JSON.parse(text);

description: A constant arithmetic expression is behaviorally safe; a pattern warning is not an injection exploit.
